**Imati** (to have) is regular in the present tense:

ja **imam** · ti **imaš** · on/ona/ono **ima** · mi **imamo** · vi **imate** · oni/one/ona **imaju**

Like Italian **avere** and French **avoir** (and unlike German **sein**), Croatian uses *imati* for age: **Imam ... godina** (I am ... years old — literally "I have ... years").

One genuine irregularity: negating *imati* isn't "ne" + *imam* — the two fuse into a single irregular verb, **nemati**: **nemam, nemaš, nema, nemamo, nemate, nemaju**. **Nemam vremena** means "I don't have time."

exercises.prompt: ___ dvadeset godina. (I am 20 years old — literally "I have 20 years".)
Koliko godina ___? (How old are you? — informal "ti")
How do you say "I don't have time"?
